sections.heading: What is 2D / Grid Dynamic Programming?
sections.content: In 2D DP the state needs two indices, so the answers live in a table dp[i][j]. The two indices can be a row and a column in a grid (dp[r][c] = best result for reaching cell (r, c)), positions in two sequences, the two ends of an interval (dp[l][r]), or an index plus a second parameter such as the number of transactions. Each cell is computed from a few neighboring cells that were filled earlier, so the whole table costs O(rows * cols) time. This topic focuses on grid paths, square and triangle tables, interval DP and tables with an extra dimension. Two-string problems such as LCS and Edit Distance, and knapsack, have their own topics.

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: Count paths or find the cheapest path in a grid when you can only move right and down
A cell's answer depends on its top, left or diagonal neighbors
Find the largest square or rectangle made of 1s in a matrix
Triangle or pyramid shapes where each row depends on the one below or above
Substring questions where dp[i][j] describes the substring from i to j (palindromes)
Interval problems where you split a range [l, r] at some point k (burst balloons)
A second parameter limits the answer (at most k transactions, k moves left)
Keywords: grid, matrix, paths, minimum path sum, obstacles, square, triangle, substring, interval

sections.heading: The Intuition
sections.content: A grid is a map and dp[r][c] is a note on each cell that says 'the best way to get here'. Because you can only arrive at a cell from the cell above or the cell to its left, its note is built from those two neighbors. Start with the corner you know (the start cell), fill the first row and column, then sweep through the rest. Every note is written once and used by the cells that come after it.

Space Optimization Rules for 2D DP
items: If dp[r][c] uses only the previous row, keep one row (or two rows) instead of the whole table
If it also uses dp[r - 1][c - 1], save the old value of dp[c - 1] in a temporary variable before overwriting it
If it uses cells from several earlier rows, or you must rebuild the path, keep the full table
Interval DP usually needs the full table because each cell reads from many cells
Always compute the optimized version only after the full-table version is correct

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Filling the table in the wrong order, so a cell reads a value that is not ready yet
Forgetting to initialize the first row and first column (or the padding row and column)
Mixing 0-indexed grid coordinates with 1-indexed dp coordinates when the table has extra padding
Swapping rows and columns when sizing arrays, such as Array(cols) { IntArray(rows) }
Overwriting a value in a rolling array before the cell that needs it has read it
Treating Dungeon Game as a forward problem; the minimum health must be computed backward
Using greedy (always pick the smaller neighbor) instead of a full DP for path problems
Int overflow in counting problems; use Long or a modulo
Trying O(n³) interval DP for n larger than about 500

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: 2D DP stores an answer for each pair of indices, such as a grid cell, an interval or (item, limit)
A grid cell is usually built from its top, left and sometimes diagonal neighbors
Set the first row and column carefully, or add a padding row and column
Fill in an order that guarantees dependencies are computed first
If a row depends only on the previous row, keep one rolling row to save memory
Interval DP tries each split point, and thinking about the LAST action often makes the pieces independent
